goal: Ship dynamic Codex terminal management with safe, isolated Git branches and worktrees for each agent workspace.
release_principles: A terminal session and a Git workspace are separate resources.
Removing a terminal never deletes its branch or worktree.
Destructive Git operations require an explicit user action and safety validation.
Automatic merge, rebase, push, pull, and branch deletion are out of scope for 0.2.0.

tasks.title: Define the 0.2.0 scope and workspace safety rules
acceptance_criteria: The user workflows for adding and removing terminals and assigning Git workspaces are documented.
Terminal removal, worktree removal, and branch deletion are defined as separate operations.
Out-of-scope behavior is documented, including automatic merge, rebase, push, pull, agent linking, branch deletion, and additional CLI tools.

tasks.title: Design the dynamic terminal and Git workspace model
acceptance_criteria: The model defines stable session IDs, labels, process state, project path, repository root, branch, worktree path, and Agenza ownership metadata.
Terminal lifecycle and Git workspace lifecycle have separate state transitions and ownership boundaries.
The persisted state schema is versioned and documented without storing terminal content or secrets.

tasks.title: Refactor the terminal process layer for dynamic sessions
acceptance_criteria: The terminal manager can create, list, restart, and remove sessions using generated IDs instead of two fixed IDs.
Input, output, resize, exit events, and IPC validation remain isolated by dynamic session ID.
Removing or disposing a session terminates its complete process tree without affecting other sessions.

tasks.title: Build the dynamic terminal workspace interface
acceptance_criteria: The user can add terminals and remove any selected terminal from the interface.
The layout remains usable with zero, one, two, and several terminal panes without a hard-coded two-pane structure.
Each pane keeps independent controls, active state, process state, and a stable user-facing label.

tasks.title: Persist and restore the terminal workspace layout
acceptance_criteria: Terminal definitions, labels, ordering, and assigned workspace metadata are stored locally using the versioned schema.
A first launch starts with a useful default layout, while later launches restore the previous layout.
Missing or inaccessible restored paths are shown safely without preventing other terminals from loading.

tasks.title: Add read-only Git repository and worktree discovery
acceptance_criteria: Agenza can identify a selected folder's repository root, current branch, and worktree state using bounded Git commands.
Local branches and registered worktrees can be listed without changing repository state.
Folders without Git and missing Git installations produce concise terminal-local errors.

tasks.title: Plan and validate branch and worktree assignments
acceptance_criteria: New branch names and worktree paths are validated with Git before any mutation occurs.
Agenza detects branch-name conflicts, branches already checked out elsewhere, duplicate paths, and unsupported repository states.
The user sees the base branch, target branch, and worktree path before confirming creation.

tasks.title: Create a branch and worktree for a terminal
acceptance_criteria: The user can create a new local branch from a selected base and assign its new worktree to one terminal.
The terminal starts Codex with the created worktree as its working directory while other terminals remain unchanged.
Partial failures roll back only resources created by the failed operation and preserve pre-existing Git data.

tasks.title: Attach an existing branch or worktree to a terminal
acceptance_criteria: The user can attach a registered worktree to a terminal without recreating it.
The user can create a worktree for an eligible existing local branch after previewing the target path.
Branches already checked out in another worktree and paths assigned to another terminal are handled without mutation or crashes.

tasks.title: Show terminal repository and workspace status
acceptance_criteria: Each terminal clearly shows its label, repository, branch, and worktree path.
The user can refresh read-only Git status and see whether the worktree has tracked, untracked, or conflicted changes.
A status failure in one terminal does not affect any other terminal or Codex process.

tasks.title: Remove terminals without deleting Git workspaces
acceptance_criteria: Removing a terminal terminates only its process tree and removes only its saved terminal definition.
The assigned branch, worktree directory, and repository registration remain untouched.
The interface clearly explains that removing a terminal does not delete Git work.

tasks.title: Add explicit safe cleanup for Agenza-created worktrees
acceptance_criteria: Worktree cleanup is a separate confirmed action available only for worktrees recorded as created by Agenza.
Cleanup refuses dirty, untracked, conflicted, locked, missing, or actively assigned worktrees instead of forcing removal.
Successful cleanup unregisters and removes the worktree but never deletes its Git branch automatically.

tasks.title: Recover safely from stale workspace state
acceptance_criteria: Externally moved or deleted worktrees, branches, and repositories are detected during restore and refresh.
Agenza offers non-destructive detach or reassignment recovery without silently pruning Git metadata.
Application restart and crash recovery do not leave terminal processes running or corrupt persisted workspace state.

tasks.title: Extend keyboard and accessibility behavior for dynamic panes
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard focus cycles predictably through any number of terminals after additions, removals, and reordering.
Add, remove, branch, worktree, and recovery controls have accessible names, focus states, and status announcements.
Terminal keyboard shortcuts remain isolated from application workspace shortcuts.

tasks.title: Add Git workspace logging and user-facing error handling
acceptance_criteria: Git discovery and mutation failures provide concise recovery actions scoped to the affected terminal.
Logs record safe workspace lifecycle metadata without terminal content, commands containing secrets, remote credentials, or environment values.
Git command timeouts and unexpected output cannot freeze or crash the whole application.

tasks.title: Add automated tests for dynamic terminals and Git workspaces
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover dynamic session creation, routing, removal, persistence, restore, focus, and complete process cleanup.
Temporary Git repositories test discovery, new and existing branch worktrees, conflicts, dirty-state refusal, cleanup, and stale recovery.
A packaged smoke test adds and removes terminals assigned to isolated worktrees and verifies no orphaned processes.

tasks.title: Perform manual 0.2.0 workspace release testing
acceptance_criteria: Zero, one, two, and several terminal layouts remain usable across restart and restore.
Two Codex agents complete independent workflows on different branches and worktrees of the same repository.
Terminal removal preserves Git work, safe cleanup refuses dirty worktrees, and app shutdown leaves no orphaned processes.

tasks.title: Create and validate the 0.2.0 distributable build
acceptance_criteria: Application and installer metadata use version 0.2.0 and the Windows installer is generated successfully.
An existing 0.1.0 user can install or run 0.2.0 without corrupting local state or Git workspaces.
The packaged app opens dynamic Codex terminals and explains missing Codex or Git prerequisites.

tasks.title: Finish 0.2.0 usage, safety, and troubleshooting documentation
acceptance_criteria: The README explains dynamic terminal management and new/existing branch and worktree workflows.
Worktree ownership, terminal removal, safe cleanup, recovery, and out-of-scope Git operations are documented clearly.
The changelog, release notes, known limitations, and troubleshooting guidance are ready for publication.

tasks.title: Prepare and publish release 0.2.0
acceptance_criteria: All release checks pass from the merged clean main commit.
The v0.2.0 tag and GitHub Release are created from the validated commit.
The validated installer and release notes are published and the 0.2.0 todo is archived.
